title_eng: Design of the Wearable Device for Hemiplegic Gait Detection Using an Accelerometer and a Gyroscope
title_kor: Design of the Wearable Device for Hemiplegic Gait Detection Using an Accelerometer and a Gyroscope
abstract:
Abstract— Hemiplegic walking is the main symptom of 
hemiplegia and is the basis for judging the outcome or severity 
of hemiplegia. In this study, we developed a wearable 
measurement module for measuring the inertia signal generated 
during walking and evaluated the p ossibility of gait 
measurement as a basic study of the new hemiplegia diagnosis 
technology using wearable device. The developed measurement 
module is worn on the waist. It is equipped with 3 -axis 
acceleration sensor and 3-axis angular velocity sensor and has 
the function to transmit and record data through wireless 
communication. As a result of measuring the gait signals using 
the developed measurement module, specific patterns are shown 
for each axis according to each step, and it is confirmed that gait 
signals can be distinguished intuitively. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Strokes occur due to problems with the blood supply to the 
brain. Strokes leading to cerebral infarction and cerebral 
hemorrhage is a serious neurological disorder causing mental 
and physical damage. Hemiplegia, which is the most common 
symptom of strokes, paralyzes one side of the body and 
triggers a biased gait pattern [1]. Gait refers to repetitive 
movements that move forward maintaining balance and 
stability through both legs, multiple muscles and joints. It is 
one of the most basic factors in evaluating the quality of 
human life. Therefore, gait recovery is a major objective in the 
rehabilitation of patients who experience stroke, it becomes an 
important indicator of the exercise of the patient’s motor 
ability [2, 3].

restoration of the hemiplegic patient in clinical trials is mainly 
dependent on observation methods such as MMT (Manual 
Muscle Testing), MAS (Modified Ashworth Scale) currently. 
However, this method is also difficult to observe the progress 
of hemiplegia in the general environment because it requires 
complicated experimental procedures and examination by a 
skilled expert. As an alternative method, accelerometer-based 
research that substitute the wired marker -based motion 
tracking with the wireless accelerator module have regarded as 
an effective gait analysis technology. Accelerator based 
method is a suitable in analyzing spatiotemporal characteristic 
of gait because it is lightweight, portable, low price and easy to 
use [5, 6]. Also, imbalance of gait pattern could be recorded 
with inertial sensor such as an accelerometer and a gyroscope. 
For example, hemiplegic gait pattern could be presented as 
differences of acceleration or angular velocity between left 
and right side steps. Therefore, an abnormal gait pattern might 
be observed with 3-axis accelerometer and 3-axis gyroscope; 
directional movement such as the walking speed and angular 
movement such as angular fluctuating asymmetry could be 
measured accelerometer and gyroscope, respectively. 
Recently, various studies have been conducted using a variety 
of sensors including acceleration sensor and gyr o sensor. 
Sagawa [7] measured horizontal and vertical distance with a 
module mounted on waist including three axes acceleration 
sensor and three axes gyro sensor regardless of the gait 
characteristics. Moe-Nilssen [8] measured the change of 
acceleration in the center of gravity of the body with respect to 
the condition of back pain using an acceleration sensor. The 
purpose of this research is t o design an unconstrained 
wearable system for hemiplegic gait detection in daily life. 
Hemiplegia paralyze one side of the body and cause a biased 
gait pattern. Moreover, aggravation of the hemiplegia could 
make a difference larger between each side of gait. Therefore, 
it is possible to estimate the severity of hemiplegia by 
observing gait pattern [9, 10]. 
II. SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT 
A. Overview of the System 
In this study, a wearable system based on a 6-axis inertia 
sensor was developed to measure the movement of gait. We 
developed an inertia sensing module and fabricated it as a 
waist band type wearable device to attach the developed 
device to the body. The developed system consists of sensing 
module for measuring and transferring 6-axis inertial signal, 
firmware for controlling MCU (micro controller unit), 
customized wearable apparatus and PC . Three axis 
accelerations and three axis angular rates are sampled on 
wearable device, and then transferred to the laptop by 
Bluetooth communication. Thus, we also developed a PC 
application that can store and display measured signals in
